questions.q: What is the primary biological purpose of aerobic cellular respiration in living organisms?
a: To release energy from glucose for cellular activities
To produce oxygen gas for breathing
To absorb sunlight to make starch
To eliminate water from body tissues

questions.q: Which chemical equation correctly summarizes aerobic cellular respiration?
a: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon dioxide + Water (+ Energy)
Water + Carbon dioxide -> Lactic acid + Oxygen

What word or term describes the process of physical breathing (inhaling and exhaling air)?
Which muscular sheet separates the thorax (chest cavity) from the abdomen and plays a vital role in ventilation?
What happens to the external intercostal muscles and ribs during inhalation (inspiration)?
a: They relax and move downwards and inwards
They contract, pulling the ribs upwards and outwards
They dissolve to let air pass

questions.q: What is the primary gas exchange surface in the human respiratory system where oxygen enters the blood?
How is the structure of alveoli specially adapted for efficient gas exchange?
a: They have thick muscular walls containing cartilage rings
They are filled with dense fluid to trap dust
They lack any blood supply to avoid blockages
They provide a massive total surface area, have walls one cell thick, and are surrounded by a dense capillary network

questions.q: What occurs to air pressure inside the thorax when the volume of the chest cavity increases during inspiration?
a: Pressure decreases below atmospheric pressure, forcing air to rush into the lungs
Pressure increases massively, pushing air out

questions.q: Which gas is present in a much higher percentage in exhaled air compared to inhaled air?
What type of respiration occurs in human skeletal muscle cells during vigorous exercise when oxygen supply becomes insufficient?
What chemical reagent is commonly used to test for the presence of carbon dioxide, turning cloudy or milky when present?
What is the main disadvantage or consequence of anaerobic respiration in human muscles compared to aerobic respiration?
a: It releases much less energy per glucose molecule and produces toxic lactic acid

questions.q: What term describes the volume of air inspired or expired with each normal breath?
Why does breathing rate and heart rate remain elevated for a short period after vigorous exercise stops?
a: To provide oxygen needed to break down and oxidize accumulated lactic acid (oxygen debt)
To store extra water in muscles

questions.q: What is the function of the rings of cartilage found along the walls of the trachea and bronchi?
a: To push food down the throat
To keep the airways open and prevent them from collapsing during pressure changes

questions.q: What is the role of goblet cells and ciliated epithelial cells lining the trachea and bronchi?
a: To trap dust and bacteria in sticky mucus and sweep it upwards away from the lungs
To pump blood through the lungs
To absorb glucose into the blood
To exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.q: How does the diaphragm behave during exhalation (expiration)?
a: It relaxes and domes upwards into the chest cavity
It vibrates rapidly to create sound
It splits into two separate muscles

questions.q: What substance builds up in human muscle cells during prolonged anaerobic respiration, causing fatigue and cramps?
Which of the following describes the composition of inspired (inhaled) atmospheric air regarding oxygen?
What happens to the volume of the thorax when a person breathes out (exhales)?
a: Volume decreases, increasing air pressure inside and forcing air out
Volume stays constant while temperature rises

questions.q: Which respiratory condition is characterized by inflammation of airways, excessive mucus production, and constriction of bronchioles, often triggered by allergens?
What is the chemical word equation for anaerobic respiration in yeast cells (fermentation)?
Why do unicellular organisms like amoeba not require a complex respiratory system or lungs?
a: They do not respire at all
They produce their own oxygen via skin pores
Their surface area to volume ratio is very large, allowing efficient gas exchange directly by diffusion across the cell membrane

questions.q: What chemical test or indicator can be used to demonstrate that living germinating seeds release heat energy during respiration?
a: A thermos flask containing a thermometer showing temperature rise
A Petri dish with iodine solution
A glass tube with biuret reagent

questions.q: What harmful substance in cigarette smoke paralyzes ciliated cells, leading to smoker's cough and bronchitis?
How does oxygen cross from the air inside an alveolus into the surrounding blood capillary?
a: Simple diffusion down a concentration gradient

questions.q: What is the term for the maximum volume of air that can be breathed out of the lungs after a maximum inhalation effort?
Which component of cigarette smoke binds strongly to haemoglobin, permanently reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity?
What is the main structural change that occurs in lungs affected by emphysema, a disease strongly linked to smoking?

questions.q: Why is the concentration of carbon dioxide higher in blood capillaries arriving at the lungs than in the alveolar air space?
a: Because lungs manufacture carbon dioxide from nitrogen
Because inhaled air contains high carbon dioxide
To maintain a concentration gradient that drives the diffusion of carbon dioxide out of the blood into the alveoli

a: They contract to pull the ribs further down and inward, decreasing chest volume rapidly
They relax to allow the lungs to fill with air

a: It remains completely clear and colorless
It turns milky / cloudy due to carbon dioxide reaction
It forms a solid yellow crystal

a: To trap dust particles like mucus
To digest bacteria entering the lungs
To provide active transport pumps for oxygen
To reduce surface tension and prevent alveoli from collapsing during exhalation

questions.q: What term describes total cellular chemical reactions occurring within an organism, including respiration?
Why do active tissues like contracting muscles require a constant, continuous supply of oxygen?
a: To enable aerobic respiration to supply sufficient ATP energy for muscle contraction
To digest lactic acid directly in the stomach
